traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Plumbaginaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins usually pinnate, rarely palmate or parallel; blades linear or oblong; stipules present or absent; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems usually herbaceous, sometimes woody; flowers in panicles, in heads or in racemes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule or nut; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 5; carpels 5. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves spiralled.

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Limonium (read 2026-10-17): ~600 spp, flowers on branched panicles or corymbs; Limonium alone is over half the family. Wikipedia Acantholimon (read 2026-10-17): 321 spp on short simple or branched flowering stems, loose or dense (type not named, so spike only raised to sometimes). Armeria (thrift, ~100 spp, dense heads) keeps head second. Panicle leads clearly. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia Limonium (read 2026-10-17): fruit a small one-seeded capsule held in the persistent calyx; Limonium (~600 spp) is over half the family. Acantholimon's page (321 spp) does not give the fruit, so it is not counted; capsule leads on Limonium alone. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves often basal, alternate, spiralled; FOC alternate or basal.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of China vol. 15 (1996), Plumbaginaceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves simple.

traits.stipules.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stipules absent; FOC stipules absent.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): margins entire or lobed; FOC entire or rarely pinnately lobed.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Flora of China vol. 15 (1996), Plumbaginaceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaf blade entire or rarely pinnately lobed.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers radially symmetric.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals 5 joined into a 5- or 10-ribbed tube; petals 5.

traits.perianth_fused.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals nearly distinct, joined at the base or for most of their length (Plumbago's corolla salverform); FOC petals connate but sometimes only at the base.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals 5, petals 5, stamens 5.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 5, opposite the petals (FOC).

traits.carpels.note: Flora of China vol. 15 (1996), Plumbaginaceae family account (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): styles 5, free or connate; stigmas 5; ovary 1-locular with 1 ovule.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): ovary superior.

traits.hypanthium.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perianth and androecium hypogynous.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals persistent in mature fruits; FOC capsules usually enclosed in the calyx.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers bisexual.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): herbs or shrubs, perennial or rarely annual.
